# Ethics of the Citizen

## By the end of today

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
You will be able to treat voting as a moral act — the delegation of coercive force — and apply reciprocity to that choice.
:::

## Where this fits

We began with ethics and force.

We end with the citizen who hires that force.

## Delegation

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
Does handing someone else the switch change the ethical problem?
:::

## Who is the client?

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
If government derives just power from consent, we are the clients.
:::

## Brennan's image

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.5em;"}
"The symbol of democracy is not just the ballot — it is the ballot connected to a gun."
:::

— Jason Brennan, *The Ethics of Voting*

## Reciprocity

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.4em;"}
"What is hateful to you, do not do to your neighbor."
:::

— Hillel the Elder

## Reciprocity and voting

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.4em;"}
What is hateful to you, do not vote for the government to do to your neighbor.
:::

## Who is the ruler?

In a democracy, the many.

True vs despotic still turns on common good versus narrow self-interest — now the voters' interest.

## Right versus rightness

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
The right to vote is not the same thing as the rightness of a particular vote.
:::

## A hard case you have seen

Texas secession referendum, 1861.

A majority voted to protect slavery and accepted a predictable war.

## Brennan's challenge

No civic duty to vote every time.

If you will not do the work of knowing, consider abstaining.

Do not dress narrow self-interest up as the common good.

## If you do vote

Understand the thing at its core.

Vote to protect equal rights — including your own.

## Direct action, ethically

Is there a responsibility to do more than vote when institutions fail?

Limits: legality, prudence, free-riding, burnout, effectiveness.

## The course in one line

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
How do we live together peacefully in a society of dignified equals?
:::

## Recap

- Voting delegates force
- Reciprocity still binds
- Franchise and virtue are different questions
- That is the last content day

## Top Hat

- T/F: Criticizing a vote as unethical means the voter should lose the franchise.
- MC: Brennan's "ballot connected to a gun" is meant to emphasize:
- Likert: "Citizens have a duty to vote in every election regardless of how little they know."
- Likert: "There is sometimes a responsibility to do more than vote."
